Geometry | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Triangles

Angles in the Front Triangle

Know two angles, know the frame

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 9–10
Topic
Triangle Angle Relationships
Standards
HSG-CO.C.10, 8.G.A.5, HSG-MG.A.1

Students use the triangle angle sum theorem, the exterior angle theorem and the base angles of isosceles triangles to find missing angles, including the angles in a bike frame.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Use the triangle angle sum theorem to find a missing angle.
  • Use the exterior angle theorem.
  • Use the base angles theorem for isosceles triangles.
  • Write and solve equations for unknown angles.

3Essential question

Why does knowing two angles of a triangle always tell you the third?

5MTB connection

A frame’s front triangle has an angle at the head-tube junction, one at the seat cluster and one at the bottom bracket. Designers choose two; the angle sum fixes the third.

Riders talk about “head angle” and “seat angle”, measured from the ground rather than inside the triangle, but they’re linked to the triangle’s angles by straight-angle and parallel-line facts.

The mathOn the trail
Angle sum = 180°Two frame angles fix the third
Exterior angleAn angle measured outside the frame triangle
Isosceles base anglesA symmetric triangular truss
Equation in xA design spec with an unknown
